thesis: This episode argues that Carvana's acquisition of Adessa creates a differentiated business model by removing decision frictions and providing the real estate capacity to sell approximately three million cars annually. The speaker views this vertical integration as a source of economic advantage, noting that while current sales are around 440,000 cars, the infrastructure supports significant future growth.

claims.claim: The speaker believes vertical integration through the Adessa acquisition provides economic advantages, removes decision frictions, and creates a differentiated business model.
claims.quote: So we thought that that acquisition was going to put us in a position to have a very differentiated infrastructure and an even more differentiated business model through more vertical integration. So we were tremendously excited about that acquisition.

claims.claim: The speaker states that after the Adessa acquisition, the company has real estate capacity to sell about three million cars per year.
claims.quote: Now with Odessa, we have real estate capacity to sell about three million cars per year. And that's certainly inside of our aspirations over time.
